name: Oak Cask Malbec
description: From one of Argentina's oldest wineries, founded in Mendoza in 1883. Part of the wine rests in oak casks, which rounds out Malbec's dark fruit.
notes: Plum, blackberry and violet, with vanilla and a little spice from the oak.
credit: NMS_FW, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Rioja
description: Bodegas Beronia was founded in Rioja Alta in 1973. A classic, easygoing Rioja built around Tempranillo, Spain's great red grape.
notes: Red cherry, strawberry and a soft touch of vanilla.
credit: Nigab Pressbilder, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Viña Tondonia 6º Año
description: A legendary traditional house in Haro, founded in 1877, famous for ageing its wines for years before release. This is an older bottling, likely from the 1970s, wrapped in the classic gold wire netting.
notes: Dried cherry, leather, tobacco and forest floor. Silky and savory with age.
credit: Geographer, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Grenache Shiraz
description: Named after the creek in the Barossa Valley where Johann Gramp planted his first vines in 1847. Grenache brings bright fruit, Shiraz a little spice: an easygoing everyday red.
notes: Raspberry, red cherry and a touch of pepper. Soft and juicy.
credit: Pernod Ricard, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Chardonnay
description: Australia's best-known Chardonnay: sunny, generous and medium-bodied, with just a kiss of oak.
notes: Melon, white peach and citrus with a creamy finish.
pairing: Roast chicken, creamy pasta, grilled fish
credit: Pernod Ricard, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Primeur Blanc
description: From the Cheylan family's estate in Provence. A primeur is released young, just weeks after the harvest, to be enjoyed while it's fresh.
notes: Fresh pear, citrus and white flowers. Light and lively.
credit: Chateau virant, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Sauvignon Blanc
description: A modern Israeli winery, founded in 2000, working with grapes from the cooler hills of the Galilee.
notes: Grapefruit, passion fruit and fresh herbs, with zesty acidity.
pairing: Grilled fish, hummus and mezze, green salads
credit: Drinking, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Rosé Tendre
description: Grown on the sandy coastal vineyards of the Camargue in southern France. Tendre means soft: a gently fruity, easy-drinking rosé.
notes: Strawberry, raspberry and candied citrus. Soft and lightly sweet.
pairing: Summer salads, grilled shrimp, fruit desserts
credit: Joséphine Gauchet, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Shiraz Rosé
description: A bright, juicy rosé made from Shiraz, Australia's signature red grape.
notes: Watermelon, cherry and red berries. Fresh and crisp.
credit: Pernod Ricard, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Ultra D Extra Brut
description: A Champagne house from the Côte des Bar, in the south of the region. Extra brut means very little sugar is added, so it's dry, pure and precise.
notes: Citrus, white flowers and fresh brioche, with fine, lively bubbles.
credit: Champagnedevaux, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Chardonnay Pinot Noir Brut Cuvée
description: Made from the two classic Champagne grapes and fermented a second time in the bottle, as the neck label says.
notes: Green apple, citrus and a hint of brioche. Fine bubbles and a crisp, dry finish.
credit: Jacob's Creek, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Sauternes (375 ml)
description: A Premier Cru in the famous 1855 Bordeaux classification. Sauternes is made from grapes shrivelled by noble rot, which concentrates their sugar into a rich, honeyed wine.
notes: Apricot, honey, candied orange and saffron.
pairing: Foie gras, blue cheese, fruit tarts
credit: Tomas er, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Sauternes (375 ml)
description: A Premier Cru Sauternes owned by the Rothschild family of Château Lafite since 1984. Golden, rich and built to age for decades.
notes: Mango, pineapple, honeycomb and toasted almond.
pairing: Roquefort, crème brûlée, spicy Asian dishes
credit: Tomas er, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
